upgrade_notice.1.10.1: Housekeeping. A retired file that no longer had any caller is gone, the two brand images are refreshed, and the directory listing gains a donate link. Nothing in the plugin behaves differently; a site on 1.10.0 loses nothing by waiting.
upgrade_notice.1.10.0: The plugin now speaks six languages — English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, German and Arabic — and brings them with it rather than waiting for a language pack. It follows your site's language by itself, falls back to French for a language it does not have, and can be set outright under Settings → Language. The booking form, the emails, the door station, the admin screens, the dates and the printed ticket are all covered, and Arabic is drawn properly on the ticket itself. Nothing to reconfigure.
upgrade_notice.1.9.1: The plugin is now Events and Tickets with QR Check-in in the directory, and Events & Tickets on your own screens. Same plugin, same folder, same settings, same data — only the name has changed, and nothing needs reinstalling or reconfiguring.
upgrade_notice.1.9.0: Adds a Help screen inside the plugin, and brings the directory page up to date: the screens are shown at last, the description covers everything added since 1.2.1, and the FAQ has been rewritten. (1.9.1 renamed the plugin again the same day — see above.)
upgrade_notice.1.8.3: Fixes a white screen when finishing the assistant, and gives it proper Back and Continue buttons — one question at a time instead of everything at once. Update before using it: in 1.8.2 the last click still failed.
upgrade_notice.1.8.2: Fixes "Security check failed" when finishing the assistant. Update before using it — in 1.8.0 and 1.8.1 the last button could not save.
upgrade_notice.1.8.1: Creating an event no longer asks for a price and a capacity on its own step — the assistant asks for them, together with the room they belong to. Three steps instead of four, and the assistant opens straight after.
upgrade_notice.1.8.0: New: an assistant that sets up an event by asking what kind of night it is. It fills in the places, the zones, the prices and when the ticket goes out, and everything it sets stays editable exactly where it always was.
upgrade_notice.1.7.0: One tab now holds the price, the capacity and the room: Prices & places. "Pricing & capacity" is gone, and the menu moved to Information & details. Nothing was lost and no setting needs re-entering. Also fixes a booking form that came back filled in, with a dead button, after the browser's back button.
upgrade_notice.1.6.1: Fixes zone prices. If your event is priced by named zones, every zone was shown and charged at the price of the event instead of its own. Worth updating before your next sale.
upgrade_notice.1.6.0: Everything the private build does, this plugin now does: the ticket studio, the floor plan editor, price categories and discount codes. Nothing is held back and nothing is capped. Existing settings and data are untouched.
upgrade_notice.1.5.0:
Zone prices reach the booking page. An event with named zones — A at 40, B at 60, C at 80 — showed every guest the same price, because the booking form had never been told the zones existed. It is told now: each guest picks a zone, pays its price, and sees how many places it has left. A zone with no price of its own costs what the event costs.

This is the same link the plugin already used to tie a ticket category to a part of the room, followed in the other direction: the room is what tiers an event that nothing else tiers, and it always could.
upgrade_notice.1.4.0:
Seating is in this plugin now. The floor that shows the evening filling, the screen that seats a booking, the button that places a party for you — all of it. Only the drawing of a floor plan stays out: the canvas, the curved rows, the round tables, the guest picking their own seat on a map. Managing places and drawing a room are two different things, and only the second one was ever worth holding back.

Fixed: an event set to "you decide where they sit" decided for you. 1.3.3 placed bookings automatically where no seating screen existed, which was a fix for one problem and a worse bug in its own right: the ticket went out before you had looked. Now only "ticket straight away" places on its own — and the screen you were being sent to actually exists.

A zone says what it controls, not whether its seats are numbered. The question an organizer really answers about a part of a room is do I care where these people sit, or only that they are in?

  • Access only — the door counts people in and nobody is told where to sit. A standing area, and equally a seated one where people sit where they like: a party, a concert, a school hall. Chairs may well exist; naming them on a ticket for a room nobody is directed in only invites an argument.
  • Numbered places — every place is named and handed out in order, nearest the stage first, and printed on the ticket.

One event can mix all of them, which is the point: a standing area, free seating behind it, and a numbered block for invited guests.

A zone with no price of its own costs what the event costs, and the field now shows that price rather than sitting empty. And a room that adds up to more places than the event says it holds now says so — one of the two numbers is wrong, and the door will believe the room.
upgrade_notice.1.3.4:
Fixed: "Confirm payment and send the tickets" was greyed out for good. 1.3.3 added a rule that holds a ticket until every guest has a place, and hung it on the wrong button. Confirming a payment records something that has already happened at a desk; it cannot be refused because a seat is undecided. The button is never disabled now — it says Confirm the payment when the tickets will have to wait, and the reason is printed under it.

And the rule no longer has a door with no key. This plugin has no screen for placing guests by hand, so being told "give everyone a place first" was being told to do something it never offered. Where there is no way to place by hand, the plugin now places the booking itself as the payment lands. If it cannot — no free place left in the category somebody paid for — it says exactly that, and the fix is in your own hands: add places to the room and the tickets go out on their own.

A paid booking whose tickets never went out now has a button that finishes it. Send them now, on the booking, once nothing is holding them.
upgrade_notice.1.3.3:
Fixed: a card payment sent tickets with no place on them. The rule that holds a ticket until every guest has a place lived in a module this plugin does not include, so an event with a room issued tickets the moment the money landed — with the place blank. The rule now lives with the room itself, which means it applies here. The guest is told their payment arrived, and the ticket follows when you have decided where they sit.

"Ticket straight away" now actually places the booking. It was a promise with nothing behind it. The plugin now gives every guest a place as the payment lands — in a category their ticket pays for, keeping the party together where the seats allow — and only then sends the ticket. If somebody cannot be seated in the category they paid for, nobody is moved and the booking waits for you: half a placed booking is worse than none.

Fixed: "This form stays open for ." with nothing in the gap. The sentence waited for a script to fill it in, and read as broken whenever anything stopped that script. The server writes it out in full now, and the script only turns it into a live clock when it can.

Fixed: WordPress's own footer line printed across the last panel of an event screen, under the sticky save bar. Room is made for it.
upgrade_notice.1.3.2:
A ticket category is tied to a part of the room. The plugin still works it out from the names on its own — "Standard admission" finds "Standard" — but the guess is only made when exactly one part of the room fits, and the Pricing screen now has a column to say it outright when the names are too far apart.

And a part of the room that a category sells is closed to every other category. This is the half that was missing. Matching alone answers "where may this guest sit?", and when the two screens were named differently it has to answer "anywhere" — which hands a standard ticket the VIP row. Claiming answers the other question, "who is this row for?", and that one can always be answered. A guest whose ticket matches nothing may now sit anywhere nobody else has claimed: never in the VIP row, and never nowhere.

Capacity and price follow the same link. A category of tickets takes its remaining places from the part of the room it sells, and a part of the room priced at zero takes the price of the category that sells it.
upgrade_notice.1.3.1:
Fixed: the plan let you choose a place the dropdown refused. The rule that keeps a standard ticket out of a VIP row was applied to the list of places and not to the plan beside it, so the same booking could be refused a row in one place and given it in the other. It is now one rule, asked by the list, the plan, automatic placement and the server alike — and the "place anyone anywhere" box lifts all four together. A rule enforced in one of two places is not a rule.

Fixed: a room category priced at zero was sold for nothing. The screen said zero meant "the price of the event", and it did not. A price is now settled in one order wherever it is needed: what you typed on the room category, or else the ticket category of the same name, or else the price of the event.

A category on a ticket that the room does not have no longer locks a guest out. "Standard admission" and "Standard" are the same thing to an organizer and two different strings to a computer. Where the names do not meet, the plugin now says so by allowing rather than by forbidding: a guest with nowhere to sit stops an evening, and that is the worse failure.
upgrade_notice.1.3.0:
A place is a coordinate, not a name. Where somebody sits is now written the way a room is actually read: the level, then the part of the room, then the row or table, then the seat along the row. Each piece appears only when it says something — a room with one level never mentions it, and a group names itself only when another group uses the same row letters. So a row is "C", not "Straight rows-C", and two blocks that both have a row C become "SR/C" and "BAL/C". Shorter on the ticket, shorter in the door list, and it fits the column it is stored in.

Levels. A room can be built on more than one — stalls and balcony, ground floor and gallery, garden and terrace. Name the level on each zone and it becomes the first thing a ticket says. Leave it empty, as most rooms will, and it is never mentioned.

A chair at a table is found by its table. Where somebody sits around a round table is nobody's business and is no longer printed; which table it is, is. A chair in a row is found by both numbers, "Row C, seat 12", because that is how somebody finds it.

Fixed: a standard ticket could be seated in a VIP place. A guest is now offered only the places the category on their ticket pays for, and automatic placement fills each guest's own category — a party of five with one VIP among them is seated in two parts of the room rather than one. The desk can still overrule it for a swap, a favour or a wheelchair, but on purpose: there is a box to tick, and the check runs again on the way in.

Fixed: pressing back could book you twice. A booking form may now be sent once, within a window you set (fifteen minutes by default), and the page shows the time left. Going back and submitting again shows the guest the booking they already have instead of making a second one — which also means a guest who has just paid cannot go back and reserve the same places again for free.

Fixed: the paid confirmation did not say who bought what. A party of five with one VIP among them was told the total and nothing else. The email now lists each guest and their category.

The printed door list keeps a clear gutter between the place and the ticket number, and prints the readable coordinate rather than the key.
upgrade_notice.1.2.2:
Fixed: the Stripe key would not save. Pasting a secret key changed nothing and the card option stayed greyed out, because the Payments screen was not allowed to write the settings it was showing. It is now, and a module can declare settings of its own on somebody else's screen rather than having them silently dropped.

New: what one person is given. A room now says whether a booking gets a whole table, row or area, or a single chair. It is one question, asked once, on the Room tab -- and everything follows from it: what can be chosen, what goes on the ticket, and what every screen calls a place. A wedding gives out tables; a cinema, a theatre or a seminar gives out chairs; standing areas have no chairs and stay areas either way. Rooms that already exist are unchanged and keep handing out whole tables and rows.

A place is no longer always called a Table. It is called a Seat, a Table, a Row or an Area, depending on what it is -- on screen, in the export, on the ticket and on the printed door list. A room that mixes them says Place. When this plugin was written a place was always a table; it has not been for a while, and a cinema seat labelled Table is the plugin admitting it has not understood the evening.

Choosing a chair on the plan. Where a room is sold seat by seat, clicking a chair on the plan picks that chair. It used to pick the whole row the chair stood in.

The plan keeps up while you seat a party. Placing four guests one after another, the second used to be offered the place the first had just been given. The plan and the lists now account for the choices already made on the screen, without a reload.

The printed door list shrinks before it cuts. A place, a ticket number, a booking reference or a category too long for its column is set a little smaller so it fits whole, and only loses its tail if it still will not fit at the smallest readable size. "Balcony-A12" clipped to "Balco..." tells an usher nothing. The place column is wider and the guest column a little narrower.
upgrade_notice.1.2.1: Two security fixes, both found and reported by Alik. Forwarding headers such as X-Forwarded-For are no longer believed by default, so a visitor can no longer hand themselves a fresh rate limit by inventing an address; and bookings for one event now happen one at a time, so two people clicking at the same instant cannot both take the last seat. If your site is behind Cloudflare or a reverse proxy, tell the plugin so under Settings → Anti-abuse.
upgrade_notice.1.2.0: Rooms and places, card payment with Stripe, and the booking page no longer depends on you having made one. Existing events are untouched and keep working exactly as before: a room is something you add when you want one, and card payment does nothing until you enter a Stripe key of your own.

screenshots.caption: The event assistant. Fifteen kinds of night, drawn rather than listed — pick the one that looks like your room, and every answer from there decides the next question. The panel on the right builds the room as you go, and shows the prices the booking page will show and the line the ticket will print. It refuses to rebuild a room that already has bookings.

The room builder. Describe the room in numbers — rows, tables to a row, chairs to a table, levels — or draw it: drag a stage in, rectangle-select a whole row, shift-click, align, space evenly, nudge with the arrow keys. The plan you draw is the plan the guest picks from and the one you watch on the night.

Prices & places, on one panel. What a ticket will say, how places are given out, the levels, and each part of the room with the price category it is sold as and the first places it hands out. The capacity is counted from the room, not typed beside it.

The booking page. One shortcode on any page. It asks for the name of every person coming — five names for a booking of five — and it knows what is left while the form is being filled in, counting the lines above and the other people booking at the same moment.

The floor, on the night. Every part of the room on one screen, filling in real time, with three facts kept apart: sold, seated, and arrived. The pale bar is what has been sold; the solid one inside it is who has walked in.

The door check-in station. A web page on any phone, opened with a per-event door code — no app to install. Camera, photo or keypad, a live count of who is inside, and one screen per scan: let in, already inside, or not for tonight.

Every ticket issued. One per guest, with its own serial and its own QR code, the place it carries, and whether that guest has walked through the door — with the minute and the entrance they came in by.
The control room. Every event, what has sold, what is still waiting on a payment, who has arrived — and the shortcode for the event you are looking at, ready to paste.

Help, inside the plugin. The whole guide on the screen where you are stuck: a first event in ten minutes, then the assistant, the room, payment, tickets, the night, and what to do when something does not arrive. Every step links to the screen it talks about.
